# Water Capital Wire

> A free daily read on the business of water for managers, investors and operators: capital, companies, technology, infrastructure and water security, with every fact sourced and dated. Each edition has a lead story traced through the water cycle (source, treatment, use, reuse, discharge), briefs across the water economy, weekly spotlights on a company, a leader, a supplier, an innovation and an investor, a capital desk of deals and firms, a water atlas on stress, demand, infrastructure, emerging sectors and security, a watchlist of water equities, a project calculator and an events calendar. General information, not investment advice.

## Today's edition
- [Nevada's data center boom could need about 34,000 acre-feet of water a year, most of it at power plants](https://watercapitalwire.com/): November 21, 2026. An updated Desert Research Institute study says proposed Nevada data centers could use about 12,800 acre-feet of water a year for cooling by 2036, and about 21,300 more at the power plants that supply them. Supply will come from groundwater, reclamation or transfers.
- [Capital: California Water Service becomes Watermark Utilities and heads for Nevada and Oregon](https://watercapitalwire.com/#money)
- [Desalination: Saudi Water Authority cancels WABAG's $272 million Yanbu desalination award](https://watercapitalwire.com/#world)
- [Utilities: Texas regulators hold off on Aqua Texas rates and weigh a five-year phase-in](https://watercapitalwire.com/#rates)
- [Energy: Select Water closes its $700 million purchase of Pilot Water Solutions](https://watercapitalwire.com/#energy)
- [Utilities: TasWater's new sewer pricing cuts hospital charges about 70% while some customers faced 500% rises](https://watercapitalwire.com/#pricing)
